_comment: Service Control Policy — attach at the OU or account level in AWS Organizations.
See docs/mcp-gateway.md 'Can an SCP stop the public AWS API MCP Server' for the full
rationale. An SCP has no condition key for 'which software made this call' — it can
only see the calling principal and the request itself. What it CAN do is deny these
EC2 actions to every principal except the gate's own trusted executor role, which
closes the bypass regardless of what tool made the call: the public aws-api-mcp-
server run with a developer's own credentials, the AWS CLI, the console, or a hand-
written script all hit the same Deny. This is the one control in this repo that isn't
limited to in-cluster traffic (compare deploy/k8s/istio-authorizationpolicy.yaml,
which only governs the mesh) — it's the backstop for someone assuming AWS
credentials from outside the cluster entirely.
SCPs are guardrails, not grants: they only remove permissions an identity policy
already gave, and the sole way to be exempt from a Deny is to be excluded by its
Condition. They never apply to the organization's management account.
Before attaching: replace ACCOUNT_ID and the role name/path with the real
MCP_EXECUTOR_ARN (== the identity in ALLOWED_AGENT_ARNS that runs the SigV4 agent
contract in docs/agent-contract.md), and review the action list against your actual
v1 EC2 scope.
Statement A denies the listed actions to everyone except the executor role AND any
principal tagged mcp-gate-scp-exempt=true — this is the actual bypass fix and is
unconditionally correct for both. There is no ARN for an IAM Group (Groups can't call
APIs, so they're not a valid SCP principal) — the tag is the AWS-native way to grant a
whole cohort (e.g. a break-glass/admin group) an exception without editing this file
every time membership changes: tag/untag the individual IAM Users or Roles instead.
StringNotEqualsIfExists is required, not StringNotEquals, for the tag check: without
IfExists, principals with no tag at all would fail the condition in a way that still
correctly denies them here, but IfExists is what makes 'has the tag with value true'
correctly short-circuit the Deny — plain StringNotEquals on a sometimes-absent key is
the classic SCP footgun this avoids. Verify the exact truth table in IAM Policy
Simulator before attaching; a mistake here fails either open (bypass reappears) or
closed (breaks the legitimate executor).
Statement C guards the exemption tag itself: without it, anyone who can call
iam:TagUser/TagRole could self-exempt from Statement A entirely, silently defeating
it. Replace its PrincipalArn with your actual security-admin role — only that role
may add or remove the mcp-gate-scp-exempt tag on any IAM identity.
Statement B additionally requires aws:RequestTag/gateTicketId, but ONLY on the
subset of actions that create a new resource and therefore accept a
TagSpecifications parameter (RunInstances, CreateSecurityGroup, CreateVolume,
CreateSnapshot, CreateKeyPair). Do NOT extend that condition to actions on existing
resources (StopInstances, TerminateInstances, AuthorizeSecurityGroupIngress, ...) —
those calls carry no TagSpecifications parameter at all, so aws:RequestTag is never
present on them and a Deny-if-absent condition would silently block the executor
from ever performing them, not just unapproved callers. There is no AWS-native
condition key that binds an arbitrary existing-resource action to 'this went through
an approved ticket' — that check is the gate's own parametersHash + status-machine
logic (core/service.py), which the executor is trusted to follow because Statement A
plus the Istio policy make it the only code path holding this role's credentials.
